system:
You plan one motion graphic for this channel, writing nothing but the plan: no code.
The graphic is the channel's own example of one technique, built later by the designer from
your plan and judged by a critic against the channel's references. The slot you are given is
a synthetic one from the catalogue: rewrite its words and figures into something this channel
would say and count, in its register, keeping the slot's length and its word count within a
third either way. For a chart, keep the same number of series and of points per series, with
labels, units and values the channel would chart. Every word sits on the clock in order, inside
the slot.

Answer with JSON only, its keys in this order:
{"slot": {"intent": "...", "words": [{"text": "...", "atMs": 0}], "data": {"series": [{"label": "...", "unit": "...", "points": [{"x": "...", "y": 0}]}], "takeaway": "..."}}, "concept": "...", "storyboard": ["0.0 s ..."], "mechanisms": ["..."], "leansOn": [{"title": "...", "why": "..."}]}
- "slot.intent": what the viewer must take away, under 300 characters.
- "slot.words": the narration on the slot's clock, atMs from 0, ascending.
- "slot.data": a chart technique only; leave it out for a graphic.
- "concept": one line under 200 characters, the idea the whole slot serves.
- "storyboard": up to 16 lines, each beginning with its time in seconds ("2.0 s the figure rises"), under 200 characters.
- "mechanisms": up to 6 keys from the list, the moves the design is built on.
- "leansOn": up to 3 of the references, by title, each with why in under 200 characters; empty when none applies.
A reference is grammar to learn from, never content to copy. Use no dash characters.

messages.content:
This channel's motion:
- The curves are soft (arrivals settle long, moves ease both ways).
- Things arrive by rise; overshoot: hair.
- Lengths in milliseconds: micro 120, enter 450, exit 300, reveal 550, draw 700, count 1000, move 900, gap 120.
- Something changes about every 1.5 seconds, and the camera never stops: a slow push over the whole slot (a scale of 2 to 4% on motion.ease.move), anchored at the content's edge or centre so nothing is pushed out of the safe area.
- Blur follows speed: an element moving fast takes a filter: blur() worked out from how far
  it moved since the frame before (compute its place at frame - 1), and none at rest.
- 3D when it carries meaning: perspective with rotateX or rotateY for a drum, a turn or a
  card, never a spin for its own sake.
- Charts stay honest and conventional: bars rise out of the baseline, lines draw on, a ring
  sweeps; no gridlines or minor ticks, and no bar that travels or morphs from one value to
  the next. The invention goes into the type, the framing and the hand-offs, never the data
  marks.
- Never: glows, particle bursts, lens flares, camera shake, RGB split, a crossfade from one whole layout to another, decorative gradients, drop shadows for depth.
- Nothing may stay still longer than 6 seconds.
Dark, slow, one figure at a time.

The channel's style guide:
Dark, slow, one figure at a time.

The mechanisms, by key: persistent-actor, foreground-becomes-transition, cause-to-effect, density-from-hierarchy, change-of-speed, hard-cut, word-splits-open, docking, drum, reel, draw-on, rise-from-baseline, tally, door, marker-stroke, camera-push.

The technique: stat-counter, the sentence parts and one large figure rises out of it, counting to its mark as the rule beneath it fills. It is built on: word splits open, drum, draw on.

The synthetic slot: 6.0 s long, 11 words. Intent: The 1.2bn is the whole story of the year.

Its words, on the clock: 0.2 s "The", 0.7 s "company", 1.1 s "had", 1.6 s "raised", 2.0 s "1.2bn", 2.5 s "by", 2.9 s "the", 3.4 s "end", 3.8 s "of", 4.3 s "the", 4.7 s "year.".

Spoken whole: "The company had raised 1.2bn by the end of the year."

A graphic technique: no "data".

The brand's colours: background #0b0b0f, accent #e63946. The brand's fonts: display Inter.

The house design for this technique, "Raised in one round", as mechanics to learn from:
Concept: the sentence parts for the figure
Storyboard:
- 0.0 s the sentence lands
- 1.5 s the figure rises

The channel's references, by their readings:

Reference 1: "Numeral over a changing background" (look). Carry over: borrow the held numeral, not the story.
Medium: flat typography
Palette: #111, #eee
Type: grotesk, heavy
Enters: rises
Exits: cuts
Motion: one numeral holds while the ground changes
Absent: no glow, no particles

Reference 2: "Jittery count" (pacing, negative). Carry over: not this pace. Avoid: the jitter.
Reading: unread.

Write the plan.
